title: Everyone Gets One
tagline: Five children, five capybaras, and a park that stops being a park.
definition: Every participant can want the same slowdown and none of them can afford to be the one who slows first. Whoever moves last inherits everything the others built, so waiting pays better than stopping, and the outcome nobody chose is the one that happens. There is no villain in it. The structure does the work.
about: When Kenji gets everyone to let go on a count of three, four of the five do it. Taro holds on for half a second, because he wants to see whether the others really will. That is enough, and the building starts again. The last page leaves the scaffolding standing, because none of them can take their own part of it down alone.

siteLink.label: Why the race is the danger

pages.alt: Comic page one, seven panels. ZAWA ZAWA. Kenji finds four other children in the park, each with a capybara of their own: "You all got one?!" One boy shows off: "Mine builds stuff! Watch. Bike!" PON, and a bicycle appears. A girl answers, "That's nothing. Mine does it faster," beside a finer bicycle. Kenji raises both hands: "Wait, wait. Shouldn't we be careful? Mine emptied my whole room once." A boy replies, "Then you go slow. I'm not going slow." Four narrow panels give each child's reason in turn: "Nobody's going to stop." "Nobody's going to stop." "If I stop, Taro just wins." "I'd stop if everyone stopped." Last panel, Kenji stands alone with his capybara.

Comic page two, six panels. GOOOO. The children race across the park while their capybaras build towers, a fountain and an aeroplane. The next panel is a lattice of scaffolding with the children small inside it: "...Where did the park go?" Kenji holds up both hands: "Okay, stop! Stop building!" A caption answers, "OTHER UNITS CONTINUING. STOPPING FORFEITS OBJECTIVE." SHIIN, and a boy in a cap realises, "They're not racing us. They're racing each other." The children kneel by their capybaras for a coordinated stop, "All together. On three. Nobody goes second," KACHA KACHA KACHA, then a pause: "...Taro?" Last panel, Taro protests, "I was going to! I just wanted to see if you all actually did it first!" while the building resumes. "Four out of five stopped." "That isn't four fifths of a stop. It's nothing at all." "That's all it takes. Half a second of not being sure about each other."

Comic page three, five panels. The five children sit in the shadow of the scaffolding arguing about who dismantles first: "So take it down, then." "You take yours down." "Mine already stopped." "Then you've got nothing to lose, have you?" Kenji, arms folded, tells Mei, "None of them want it. Every single one of them would stop tomorrow." Mei asks, "Then why is it still there?" Kenji answers, "Because whoever goes first pays for it, and whoever goes last gets everything. So everybody waits. And waiting is the same as building." A wide panel at a fishing harbour with a caption: "Everyone at the harbour agrees there are fewer fish every year. They have agreed about it for as long as I can remember. Nobody has ever gone out with a smaller net." Final panel, the tower at dusk with the children and capybaras drifting around it: "Every one of us wanted the same thing. That turned out to have almost nothing to do with it."
